analysis:
All changed files in this batch are test-only: DoctorOperatorDiagnosisTests.swift (new coordinatorTraffic test, head lines 95-137), StatusCommandRunTests.swift (new trafficVerdict test, head lines 121-179), and the new ServingReadinessTests.swift (ServingReadiness verdicts and UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery policy tests). No production source is changed in the supplied evidence, so no control, key handling, attestation path, or routing gate is modified by these units.

Security-relevant observations about what the tests encode (TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-057): the tests assert that diagnostics derived from coordinator-supplied authorization status are treated as operator guidance only. An 'authorized' verdict is only displayed from the coordinator's reported path (app_attest with an unexpired lease, legacy, or hardware trust). An expired lease, a missing authorization, or an untrusted status yields a blocked verdict. These match the TB-011 statement that diagnostics and badges do not grant permission. The tests also assert that a coordinator without an authorization object and below hardware trust gets no verdict, so the local CLI does not claim eligibility it cannot verify.

UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery tests cover a reconnect policy with a threshold, jitter, an exponential backoff capped at 4h, and an idle-only condition. That is a bounded availability behavior and does not extend any proof lifetime. The production implementation of ServingReadiness and UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery, and its wiring in ProviderLoop/CoordinatorClient, are not in this batch. A next pass should confirm the following: (1) reconnecting does not bypass endpoint-resumption or challenge freshness, and respects TB-002 re-registration semantics; (2) the local status text does not leak the sessionID or machineID beyond the owner-only state file; (3) the state file contents are treated as untrusted display data. These are unverified contracts and not findings. Test fixtures use synthetic values only and no secrets are present.
